newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Stolen uranium seized in Lithuania.
newsitem.headline: Stolen uranium seized in Lithuania.

text.p: Lithuanian security officials said on Thursday that they had seized around 70 kg (154 lbs) of radioactive uranium stolen from the Baltic state's Ignalina nuclear power plant five years ago.
Officials seized 20 kg (44 lbs) of nuclear fuel on Tuesday near Ignalina and another 50 kg (110 lbs) near the capital Vilnius on Wednesday.
The seizures are part of a haul of 100 kg (220 lbs) of nuclear fuel stolen from Ignalina in 1992. Most of the uranium has now been recovered and officials believe the rest has been sold.

Lithuania has been under intense Western scrutiny over security and safety at Ignalina, which houses the largest of the Chernobyl-style RBMK reactors, responsible for the world's worst nuclear disaster in 1986.
"The work we have been doing for the past three years is coming to its completion," said Vytautas Pociunas, who heads the investigation into the stolen uranium.
"We have discovered most of the uranium stolen from Ignalina nuclear power plant," he added.
He said the uranium was radioactive but had not polluted the environment as it had not leaked.
Pociunas said three people would go on trial for the theft. All are former security guards at Ignalina.
A plant engineer was questioned but was released due to lack of evidence and has since fled Lithuania.
"We have nearly all the information now and I think the case will be passed to court in the next few months," Pociunas said.
